html:
The Republic of the Congo civil war began in June 1997 in Brazzaville, between the forces of President Pascal Lissouba and the Cobra militia of former president Denis Sassou Nguesso.

Each leader had his own militia drawn from his home region. When the army tried to disarm Sassou's men, fighting spread through Brazzaville, which was largely destroyed. In October Angolan troops entered on Sassou's side and he took power.

Fighting went on in the Pool region south of the capital into 1999, with many thousands killed and hundreds of thousands displaced. The war ended the democratic years begun in 1992 and gave Sassou Nguesso a hold on power he still keeps. It was tied to the wars in Angola and the Congo next door.
sum: The Republic of the Congo civil war began in June 1997 in Brazzaville, between the forces of President Pascal Lissouba and the Cobra militia of former president Denis Sassou Nguesso.
